title: Serbo-Croatian Latin (Croatian, Bosnian, Serbian, Montenegrin) — practical English/ASCII
authority: English-language press and informal 'ošišana latinica' convention (no official status)
description: Folds Gaj's Latin to ASCII the way English-language media do: č/ć→c, š→s, ž→z, dž→dz, đ→dj (Đoković → Djokovic); lj/nj stay. Accepts the Unicode digraph letters ǅ/ǈ/ǋ and Montenegrin ś/ź.
notes: đ→dj is the English/press convention; ICAO MRZs use D (Montenegro's 2008 MRZ rule: Đ→D). Use latin_icao for MRZ-style folding (ĐOKOVIĆ → DOKOVIC).
Digraph code points: ǆ/ǉ/ǌ map directly; the title-case forms ǅ/ǈ/ǋ are expanded by aliases to Dž/Lj/Nj (their upper-case forms Ǆ/Ǉ/Ǌ to DŽ/LJ/NJ) so that case is restored correctly.

Capital Ð (U+00D0, Icelandic eth) is aliased to Đ: the two capitals look identical and Ð is often typed for Đ in Croatian and Serbian text. Lower-case ð is left to the ICAO fallback (→ d), so Guðrún → Gudrun.
Slovene uses the same letters without ć/đ; Bosnian and Croatian use the same inventory as Serbian Latin.
Other non-ASCII letters (foreign names) are folded with the ICAO §6.A table (fallback 'ascii').
